states: Private mock stack built from this tree; Playwright page.clock installed at load, /ws held after first render (server frames dropped) and REST GETs replayed from their last response, then the clock fast-forwarded with no data change
Kubernetes workloads 1600px: Job/CronJob Detail "Completed 48m ago" / "Last success 1h ago" -> "Completed 3h ago" / "Last success 4h ago" after 3h
Kubernetes Job row expansion: controller section "01:59 PM (48m ago)" -> "01:59 PM (3h ago)" with the absolute time unchanged; Runtime context Last seen "1s ago" -> "3 hours ago"
Proxmox backups 1600px and 390px: tracked artifact "1d ago" / "1d" in the current (green) band -> "8d ago" / "8d" in the aging (amber) band, title "Aging backup age", after 7 days
Proxmox replication 1600px: row and expanded Last sync "21m ago" -> "3h ago", Next sync "in 8m" -> "2h overdue" in red after 3h; one background /api/replication/jobs read fired during the jump
Proxmox replication 390px compact row: Last sync "21m" -> "3h", Next sync "8m" -> "-2h"
Machines 1600px with Last seen column hidden: identity title "| seen just now" -> "| seen 3h ago"; 390px Seen cells "just now" -> "3h ago"

Control on the same stack with the seven runtime files swapped back to the parent: Kubernetes Detail and expansion, replication expanded Last sync / Next sync and phone row, machines subtitle, and phone backup ages stayed frozen; desktop backup text moved but the band stayed green
interactions: Clicked a Kubernetes Job controller row to open its expansion
Opened View > Choose which columns to display and unchecked Last seen on Machines
page.clock.fastForward 3h (Kubernetes, replication, machines) and 7 days (backups) with data held
